```{r}
#| label: setup
# Load packages and define one shared chart style used by every figure
library(tidyverse)
library(nycflights13)
library(broom)      # tidy model results
library(sandwich)   # clustered standard errors
library(lmtest)     # apply them to the models

theme_report <- theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.background  = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA),
    plot.title       = element_text(colour = "#0b0b0b"),
    plot.subtitle    = element_text(colour = "#52514e"),
    axis.text        = element_text(colour = "#52514e"),
    strip.text       = element_text(colour = "#0b0b0b", face = "bold")
  )

# Plain-language table headers: code column name -> label shown in the report
column_labels <- c(
  table            = "Table",
  rows             = "Rows",
  columns          = "Columns",
  column           = "Column",
  n_missing        = "Missing",
  pct_missing      = "% missing",
  status           = "Status",
  n                = "Flights",
  pct              = "% of flights",
  n_flights        = "Flights",
  mean_arr_delay   = "Mean arrival delay (min)",
  median_arr_delay = "Median arrival delay (min)",
  mean_dep_delay   = "Mean dep. delay (min)",
  median_dep_delay = "Median dep. delay (min)",
  pct_late_15      = "% late >15 min",
  pct_cancelled    = "% cancelled",
  carrier          = "Code",
  name             = "Airline",
  origin           = "Airport",
  month            = "Month",
  variable         = "Weather measure",
  level            = "Condition",
  check            = "Check",
  count            = "Count",
  measure          = "Weather measure",
  condition        = "Condition",
  model1           = "Weather only (min)",
  model2           = "+ season, hour, airport (min)",
  ci95             = "95% CI",
  odds_ratio       = "Odds ratio"
)

# Print a table with readable headers and thousands separators (336,776).
# Any column without a label keeps its original name.
show_table <- function(data) {
  labels <- coalesce(unname(column_labels[names(data)]), names(data))
  knitr::kable(data, col.names = labels,
               format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
}
```

## Introduction

This report explores the **nycflights13** dataset: every flight that departed
New York City's three main airports (JFK, LaGuardia and Newark) in 2013, plus
related tables on airlines, airports, planes and hourly weather. It looks at
data quality first, then patterns in flight delays, then how weather relates
to delays and cancellations.

## 1. The data

The package contains five tables:

```{r}
#| label: table-sizes
# Put the five tables in a named list so each can be handled the same way
tables <- list(
  airlines = airlines,
  airports = airports,
  flights  = flights,
  planes   = planes,
  weather  = weather
)

# One row per table: its number of rows and columns
imap(tables, \(tbl, name) {
  tibble(table = name, rows = nrow(tbl), columns = ncol(tbl))
}) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  show_table()
```

Most columns are complete. The columns below have missing values:

```{r}
#| label: missing-values
# Count NAs in every column of every table, then keep only columns with gaps
imap(tables, \(tbl, name) {
  tbl |>
    summarise(across(everything(), \(x) sum(is.na(x)))) |>
    pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "column",
                 values_to = "n_missing") |>
    mutate(pct_missing = round(n_missing / nrow(tbl) * 100, 1)) |>
    mutate(table = name, .before = 1)
}) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  filter(n_missing > 0) |>
  show_table()
```

The gaps in `flights` matter most: flights with no departure time are treated
as **cancelled** in the rest of this report. `planes$speed` and
`weather$wind_gust` are mostly empty, so they are not used.

## 2. Flight delays

### Flight status

```{r}
#| label: flight-status
# Label each flight: no dep_time = cancelled; departed but no arr_delay =
# diverted or incomplete record; everything else = completed
flight_status <- flights |>
  mutate(status = case_when(
    is.na(dep_time)  ~ "cancelled",
    is.na(arr_delay) ~ "no arrival data",
    .default         = "completed"
  ))

flight_status |>
  count(status) |>
  mutate(pct = round(n / sum(n) * 100, 1)) |>
  show_table()

completed <- flight_status |>
  filter(status == "completed")
```

The rest of this section uses **arrival delay** for completed flights only.
A flight counts as *late* if it arrived more than 15 minutes behind schedule
(the FAA's definition). Negative delays mean the flight arrived early.

```{r}
#| label: delay-function
# The same delay statistics for any grouping (or none), rounded to 1 decimal
summarise_delays <- function(data, ...) {
  data |>
    group_by(...) |>
    summarise(
      n_flights        = n(),
      mean_arr_delay   = mean(arr_delay),
      median_arr_delay = median(arr_delay),
      pct_late_15      = mean(arr_delay > 15) * 100,
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 1)))
}
```

### Overall

```{r}
#| label: delay-overall
summarise_delays(completed) |>
  show_table()
```

The median is well below the mean: most flights arrive on time or early, and a
smaller number of very late flights pull the average up.

### By airline

```{r}
#| label: delay-airline
# Add full airline names, worst average delay first
summarise_delays(completed, carrier) |>
  left_join(airlines, by = "carrier") |>
  relocate(name, .after = carrier) |>
  arrange(desc(mean_arr_delay)) |>
  show_table()
```

Airlines with only a few hundred flights (or fewer) have less reliable
averages than the large carriers.

### By origin airport

```{r}
#| label: delay-origin
summarise_delays(completed, origin) |>
  show_table()
```

### By month

```{r}
#| label: delay-month
summarise_delays(completed, month) |>
  show_table()
```

### By time of day

```{r}
#| label: delay-hour
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 4
# Drop hours with fewer than 100 flights so a handful of flights can't
# distort the line
by_hour <- summarise_delays(completed, hour) |>
  filter(n_flights >= 100)

ggplot(by_hour, aes(x = hour, y = mean_arr_delay)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "#c3c2b7", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_line(colour = "#2a78d6", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(colour = "#2a78d6", size = 2.5) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(5, 23, by = 2)) +
  labs(
    title    = "Average arrival delay by scheduled departure hour",
    subtitle = "Completed flights only",
    x        = "Scheduled departure hour (24-hour clock)",
    y        = "Mean arrival delay (minutes)"
  ) +
  theme_report
```

## 3. Weather and delays

Weather is recorded hourly at each of the three NYC airports, so this section
switches to **departure delay**. Each flight is matched to the weather at its
origin airport during its *scheduled* departure hour. Cancelled flights are
kept, because bad weather may be the reason they were cancelled.

```{r}
#| label: weather-join
# Clean weather: impossible wind speeds (> 100 mph) become NA; keep one
# reading per airport-hour as a safeguard (none were duplicated in testing)
weather_clean <- weather |>
  mutate(wind_speed = if_else(wind_speed > 100, NA, wind_speed)) |>
  select(origin, time_hour, precip, visib, wind_speed) |>
  distinct(origin, time_hour, .keep_all = TRUE)

# Match each flight to its origin airport's weather at the scheduled hour
flights_weather <- flights |>
  left_join(weather_clean, by = c("origin", "time_hour"),
            relationship = "many-to-one")

# Data-quality checks
tibble(
  check = c("Implausible wind speeds set to NA",
            "Flights with no matching weather reading"),
  count = c(sum(weather$wind_speed > 100, na.rm = TRUE),
            sum(is.na(flights_weather$visib)))
) |>
  show_table()
```

```{r}
#| label: weather-summary
# Put each weather measure into readable groups (each includes its lower edge)
flights_binned <- flights_weather |>
  mutate(
    precip_group = case_when(
      is.na(precip)  ~ NA,
      precip == 0    ~ "None",
      precip <= 0.1  ~ "Light (up to 0.10 in)",
      .default       = "Heavier (over 0.10 in)"
    ) |>
      factor(levels = c("None", "Light (up to 0.10 in)",
                        "Heavier (over 0.10 in)")),
    visib_group = cut(
      visib, breaks = c(-Inf, 1, 3, 10, Inf), right = FALSE,
      labels = c("Under 1 mi", "1-3 mi", "3-10 mi", "10 mi (clear)")
    ),
    wind_group = cut(
      wind_speed, breaks = c(-Inf, 10, 20, Inf), right = FALSE,
      labels = c("Under 10 mph", "10-20 mph", "20+ mph")
    )
  )

# Cancellations and departure-delay statistics for one weather grouping
summarise_by_weather <- function(data, group_col, variable_name) {
  data |>
    filter(!is.na({{ group_col }})) |>
    group_by(level = {{ group_col }}) |>
    summarise(
      n_flights        = n(),
      pct_cancelled    = mean(is.na(dep_time)) * 100,
      mean_dep_delay   = mean(dep_delay, na.rm = TRUE),
      median_dep_delay = median(dep_delay, na.rm = TRUE),
      pct_late_15      = mean(dep_delay > 15, na.rm = TRUE) * 100,
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    mutate(variable = variable_name, level = as.character(level),
           .before = 1) |>
    mutate(across(where(is.double), \(x) round(x, 1)))
}

weather_summary <- bind_rows(
  summarise_by_weather(flights_binned, precip_group, "Precipitation"),
  summarise_by_weather(flights_binned, visib_group,  "Visibility"),
  summarise_by_weather(flights_binned, wind_group,   "Wind speed")
)

show_table(weather_summary)
```

```{r}
#| label: weather-chart
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 4.5
# One panel per weather measure, shared y-axis so bars are comparable
weather_summary |>
  mutate(level = fct_inorder(level)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = level, y = mean_dep_delay)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#2a78d6", width = 0.6) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "#c3c2b7", linewidth = 0.4) +
  facet_wrap(~ variable, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(
    title    = "Mean departure delay by weather at the origin airport",
    subtitle = "Weather at the scheduled departure hour",
    x        = NULL,
    y        = "Mean departure delay (minutes)"
  ) +
  theme_report +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x        = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1)
  )
```

## 4. Separating the weather effects

Section 3 compared each weather measure on its own, but rain, low visibility
and wind often occur together, and bad weather may fall at times that are
already busy. Regression estimates each condition's link with delays **while
holding the others fixed**. Three models are fitted:

- **Model 1**: departure delay (minutes) on the three weather measures together.
- **Model 2**: Model 1 plus month, scheduled hour and origin airport.
- **Model 3**: a logistic regression of whether a flight was cancelled, with
  the same predictors as Model 2.

All results are relative to **good weather**: no precipitation, 10-mile
visibility and wind under 10 mph. Flights at the same airport in the same hour
share identical weather, so standard errors are clustered by airport-hour.

```{r}
#| label: regression-models
# Model data: reuse the weather groups from Section 3, drop the single
# hour-1 flight, set clear visibility as the baseline, and treat month,
# hour and airport as categories
model_data <- flights_binned |>
  filter(hour >= 5) |>
  mutate(
    cancelled    = is.na(dep_time),
    visib_group  = fct_relevel(visib_group, "10 mi (clear)"),
    month        = factor(month, levels = 1:12, labels = month.abb),
    hour         = factor(hour),
    origin       = factor(origin),
    weather_hour = paste(origin, time_hour)   # cluster ID
  ) |>
  drop_na(precip_group, visib_group, wind_group)

departed <- model_data |>
  filter(!cancelled)

# Fit the three models
m1_weather <- lm(dep_delay ~ precip_group + visib_group + wind_group,
                 data = departed)

m2_controls <- lm(dep_delay ~ precip_group + visib_group + wind_group +
                    month + hour + origin,
                  data = departed)

m3_cancel <- glm(cancelled ~ precip_group + visib_group + wind_group +
                   month + hour + origin,
                 family = binomial, data = model_data)

# Clustered standard errors, then a tidy table with 95% CIs
tidy_clustered <- function(model, cluster_id) {
  coeftest(model, vcov. = vcovCL(model, cluster = cluster_id)) |>
    tidy(conf.int = TRUE)
}

# Keep only the weather terms, split into measure + condition
weather_terms <- function(tidy_df) {
  tidy_df |>
    filter(str_detect(term, "_group")) |>
    mutate(
      measure = case_when(
        str_starts(term, "precip") ~ "Precipitation",
        str_starts(term, "visib")  ~ "Visibility",
        .default                   = "Wind speed"
      ),
      condition = str_remove(term, "^(precip|visib|wind)_group"),
      .before = 1
    ) |>
    select(measure, condition, estimate, conf.low, conf.high)
}

m1_terms <- tidy_clustered(m1_weather,  departed$weather_hour) |>
  weather_terms()
m2_terms <- tidy_clustered(m2_controls, departed$weather_hour) |>
  weather_terms()
m3_terms <- tidy_clustered(m3_cancel,   model_data$weather_hour) |>
  weather_terms()
```

### Delays

```{r}
#| label: regression-delay-table
# One row per condition: both models' estimates, plus Model 2's 95% CI
m2_terms |>
  left_join(m1_terms |> select(measure, condition, model1 = estimate),
            by = c("measure", "condition")) |>
  transmute(
    measure, condition,
    model1 = round(model1, 1),
    model2 = round(estimate, 1),
    ci95   = sprintf("%.1f to %.1f", conf.low, conf.high)
  ) |>
  show_table()
```

```{r}
#| label: regression-delay-chart
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 5
# Dot = estimated extra delay vs good weather; line = 95% CI.
# Two models, so two colours and a legend.
bind_rows(
  "Weather only"                    = m1_terms,
  "Weather + season, hour, airport" = m2_terms,
  .id = "model"
) |>
  mutate(condition = fct_rev(fct_inorder(condition)),
         model     = fct_inorder(model)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = estimate, y = condition, colour = model)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "#c3c2b7", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(xmin = conf.low, xmax = conf.high),
                  position = position_dodge(width = 0.6),
                  size = 0.4, linewidth = 0.7) +
  facet_grid(measure ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("#2a78d6", "#eb6834")) +
  labs(
    title  = "Extra departure delay compared with good weather",
    x      = "Extra minutes of departure delay (95% CI)",
    y      = NULL,
    colour = NULL
  ) +
  theme_report +
  theme(legend.position = "top",
        strip.text.y    = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0))
```

Every weather effect remains clearly positive after holding the others fixed.
The precipitation effect **shrinks** as other factors are added: part of the
raw rain effect in Section 3 was really low visibility, and part was season
and time of day. The effect of the **worst visibility grows** once time of day
is controlled for, possibly because fog is most common in the early morning,
the least-delayed part of the day (not verified here). Wind has the smallest
effect on delays.

Weather explains only about `r round(summary(m1_weather)$r.squared * 100)`%
of the variation in individual flight delays, rising to
`r round(summary(m2_controls)$r.squared * 100)`% with the controls. Bad weather
adds substantial delay when it occurs, but it is rare, and most delays come
from factors not in this data, such as knock-on delays, congestion and
destination weather.

### Cancellations

```{r}
#| label: regression-cancel-table
# Convert log-odds to odds ratios: 3 = three times the odds of cancellation
# compared with good weather, holding everything else constant
m3_terms |>
  transmute(
    measure, condition,
    odds_ratio = round(exp(estimate), 2),
    ci95       = sprintf("%.2f to %.2f", exp(conf.low), exp(conf.high))
  ) |>
  show_table()
```

An **odds ratio** compares the odds of cancellation with those in good
weather: 1 means no difference, 3 means three times the odds. For
cancellations the ranking changes: **very low visibility and strong wind**
are linked with the highest odds, while precipitation matters least once
visibility is accounted for. Heavier precipitation's odds ratio is not
clearly different from light precipitation's: the confidence intervals
overlap and the heavier group is small.

## 5. Summary and caveats

**Main patterns**

- Most flights arrive on time or early; average delays are driven by a
  minority of very late flights.
- **Time of day** shows the clearest pattern: early-morning flights arrive
  early on average, and delays build steadily into the evening.
- Delays are worst in early summer and December, and lowest in autumn.
- **Weather:** holding the other conditions fixed, **precipitation and very
  low visibility** add the most delay, and wind the least. For
  **cancellations**, very low visibility and strong wind matter most.

**Caveats**

- Section 4 separates the weather measures from each other and from season,
  time of day and airport, but the results are still associations, not proven
  causes: factors not in the data (such as destination weather or congestion)
  could still play a role.
- Regression estimates average extra minutes, which a small number of very
  long delays can strongly influence.
- Cancellations are inferred from a missing departure time; the data has no
  explicit cancellation flag.
- Weather is matched to the *scheduled* departure hour at the *origin*
  airport only; destination weather is not captured.
- Small airlines and rare weather conditions have fewer flights, so their
  figures are less certain.
